# Convert JPG to PDF

- Route: `/tools/convert-jpg-to-pdf`
- Kind: `tool`
- Category: `image`
- Slug: `convert-jpg-to-pdf`

## Summary

Turn JPG photos and scans into clean PDF documents ready to share, print, or upload. (Image tools)

## Details

JPG is the format your phone and camera shoot in, but a PDF is what most forms, applications, and offices want. Media Manipulator embeds your JPG directly into a PDF with no re-compression, so the document looks exactly like your photo and stays small.
### What it does
- Wraps a JPG/JPEG photo into a single-page PDF document.
- Embeds the original JPG bytes losslessly — zero added compression.
- Sizes the page to the photo so nothing is cropped or stretched.
- Produces a standard PDF that opens and prints anywhere.
### How to use it
1. Upload JPG: Drop in a .jpg or .jpeg photo or scan.
2. We embed it: The JPG is placed on a matching-size page, uncompressed.
3. Generate PDF: A standard single-page PDF is assembled.
4. Download PDF: Save a clean .pdf ready to share or upload.
### Supported formats
- Input: jpg, jpeg
- Output: pdf
- The JPG is embedded losslessly (no re-compression) into a single-page PDF.
### Technical details
- The JPG stream is embedded with the PDF /DCTDecode filter, meaning the photo is stored as-is — no second round of lossy compression.
- Because there is no re-encode, a JPG-to-PDF document is typically about the same size as the original photo.
- The page is sized from the image at 96 DPI, so a typical phone photo produces a comfortably sized page.
### Use cases
- Job applications: Turn a photo of a signed form into a PDF a portal accepts.
- Receipts and expenses: Convert receipt photos to PDFs for expense reports.
- Scanned documents: Wrap a phone scan of a page into a tidy PDF.
- Printing: Get predictable print output from a JPG.
### FAQ
Q: How do I convert a JPG to PDF for free?
A: Upload your .jpg above and click convert — the output is a single-page PDF. It is free and requires no signup.
Q: Will converting JPG to PDF lower the quality?
A: No. The JPG is embedded directly into the PDF without re-compression, so the image quality is identical to your original file.
Q: Will the PDF be much bigger than my JPG?
A: No — because there is no re-encoding, the PDF is roughly the same size as the source JPG plus a tiny document wrapper.
Q: Can I combine multiple JPGs into one PDF?
A: This tool makes one PDF per image. Convert each JPG and merge the PDFs in a merge tool if you need multiple pages.
